title: Quantification of SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater
author: David Ian Walker
materials: Decontaminate the KingFisher™ Flex Purification System to remove nucleases after each run using Thermo Scientific™ RNase AWAY™ Surface Decontaminant or a similar product.

steps.title: Prepare phi6 Process Control Working Suspension
steps.instruction: Prepare a new batch of phi6 process control working suspension on each day of testing.

substeps.instruction: Remove an aliquot of phi6 stock from the freezer (prepared according to Appendix 1), thaw, and mix thoroughly by vortexing.

Add phi6 stock to Ringer’s ¼ Strength Solution to a final volume of 50±0.5 ml, mixing thoroughly by inverting several times. Ensure the final concentration is high enough to quantify a 0.01% recovery.

steps.title: Prepare Wastewater Samples and Controls
steps.instruction: Prepare the wastewater samples and spring water controls for processing.

substeps.instruction: Mix each sample by inverting the sample bottle 10 times within a biological safety cabinet.
Measure approximately 200 mL of sample into a suitable centrifuge bottle.
Prepare at least two control centrifuge bottles with approximately 200 mL of spring water.

steps.title: Clarify Samples and Add Process Control
steps.instruction: Isolate the clarified supernatant and spike with phi6 process control.

substeps.instruction: Place the centrifuge rotor into a biological safety cabinet and remove samples, ensuring pelleted solids are not disturbed.
Carefully decant 150±1 g of clarified supernatant into clean centrifuge bottles using a digital balance, minimizing the transfer of pelleted solids.
Add 1±0.01 ml of phi6 process control to each 150 mL clarified sample and one spring water control sample; mix well by shaking or inverting.

steps.title: Concentrate Virus via Ammonium Sulphate Precipitation
steps.instruction: Concentrate the viral particles using ammonium sulphate precipitation and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Pour sample/phi6 mixtures into centrifuge bottles containing 60±1 g of ammonium sulphate (one spring water bottle with phi6 serves as the phi6 positive control, the other as the total blank control).
Dissolve ammonium sulphate by inverting bottles several times or shaking on an orbital shaker at approximately 200 rpm.
Incubate samples at 3±2°C for 60 to 180 minutes.
Mark the outer sides of the bottles where pellets will form.
Centrifuge chilled samples for 00:30:00 at 10000 x g at 4±1°C with no braking.
Place rotor in a biological safety cabinet and remove bottles without disturbing the viral pellets.
Pour off and dispose of the supernatant as biohazardous waste.

steps.title: Lysis and Pellet Resuspension
steps.instruction: Lysis the viral pellet and prepare for RNA extraction.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge samples and controls at 10000 x g for 30 minutes at ambient temperature.
Add 2 mL of NucliSENS lysis buffer (or an appropriate volume of GITC containing lysis buffer if using an alternative validated method) directly to the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet thoroughly by repeat pipetting, avoiding air introduction to prevent foaming.
If RNA extraction is not immediate, transfer the mixture to clean tubes and store at 3±2°C for up to 48 hours.

steps.title: Prepare RNA Extraction Plates
steps.instruction: Set up the 24-well deep-well plates for the KingFisher™ Flex Purification System.

substeps.instruction: Transfer lysis buffer/pellet mixture to a clean 24-well deep-well plate with a 24-tip rack; label as 'Tips and lysate'.
Add 50 µL of well-mixed NucliSENS magnetic silica beads to the corresponding wells in a second 24-well plate; label as 'Beads'. (Can be stored at 3±2°C for 7 days).
Add 385 µL of NucliSENS wash buffer 1 to two plates; label as 'Wash 1a and Wash 1b'.
Add 485 µL of NucliSENS wash buffer 2 to two plates; label as 'Wash 2a and Wash 2b'.
Add 500 µL of NucliSENS wash buffer 3 to one plate; label as 'Wash 3'.
Add 120 µL of NucliSENS wash buffer 3 to one plate; label as 'Elution'. (Wash buffer plates can be stored at 3±2°C for 7 days).

steps.title: Perform Automated RNA Purification
steps.instruction: Extract RNA using the KingFisher™ Flex Purification System.

substeps.instruction: Load the WW_Nucisens_Kingfisher_24 protocol on the system.
Load the wash buffer and sample/magnetic silica bead plates and press Start.
Recover the elution plate and cover with an adhesive cover.

steps.title: Store Purified RNA
steps.instruction: Store RNA based on the intended timeframe for use.

substeps.instruction: Store at 3±2°C for use on the same day.
Store at < -15 °C for use within 1 week.
Store at ≤ -70 °C for longer periods.

steps.title: Perform RT-qPCR Analysis
steps.instruction: Quantify SARS-CoV-2 and phi6 using RT-qPCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare RT-qPCR master mix for each sample, total blank, phi6 positive controls, at least four ssRNA standard dilutions, and TEX buffer NTC (at least 2 replicates per assay for SARS-CoV-2 and phi6).
Add master mix to PCR plate wells, leaving space for template RNA.
Add sample RNA, control template RNA, or NTC to appropriate wells (for N1 assay: 5 µL for phi6, 2 µL for others).
Add ssRNA standard dilutions to appropriate wells.
Cover plates and run RT-qPCR in a real-time PCR machine using cycling conditions from Table 4.
Note the time when the run finishes.

steps.title: Prepare Pseudomonas Host Stocks
steps.instruction: Create and store host bacterial stocks in a sterile environment.

substeps.instruction: Rehydrate a freeze-dried Pseudomonas culture (DSMZ) in 0.5 mL TSB.
Allow to rehydrate for 00:10:00, then add to 8.5 mL of TSB.
Incubate, shaking at 25±1°C overnight (18 to 24 hours) until turbid.
Add 1 mL of sterile glycerol and mix by inverting several times.
Split into 150 µL aliquots in screwcap cryovials and store at ≤ -70 °C for up to 1 year.
Note: New host stocks can be created via subculturing on TSA using a single colony, but completely new stocks must be prepared annually from freeze-dried culture.

steps.title: Prepare phi6 Stocks
steps.instruction: Cultivate and store phi6 stocks using the host culture.

substeps.instruction: Thaw an aliquot of host stock and mix gently by flicking.
Add 100 µL of host stock to 10 mL TSB in a sterile centrifuge tube; incubate, shaking at 25±1°C overnight (18 to 24 hours) until turbid.
Add 5 mL of TSB and 5 µL of 0.5 M calcium chloride solution to two centrifuge tubes.
Add 0.5 mL of overnight host culture to each tube; incubate, shaking at 25±1°C overnight (18 to 24 hours) until turbid.
Rehydrate a freeze-dried vial of phi6 in 500 µL Ringer’s ¼ Strength Solution.
Add 100 µL of phi6 suspension to one of the host culture tubes; incubate, shaking at 25±1°C overnight (18 to 24 hours).
Verify that the phi6 culture broth is clearer than the control broth.
Centrifuge the phi6 culture at 4000 to 10000 x g for 00:15:00 at 4±1°C and discard the control culture.
Add 0.8 g of sterile glycerol to two 15 ml tubes, fill each to 6 mL with the supernatant, and invert to mix.
Split into 10 µL aliquots and store at < -70 °C for up to one year.
Note: New phi6 stocks must be created annually from freeze-dried culture and should be cultured by plaque assay (per Prussin et al. 2018) rather than directly from broth.
